issues.description: The manuscript states in the Procedure section (2.5) that the individual memory test will contain '20 open-ended questions' and describes four indices derived from open-ended responses. However, in the Analysis Plan (Section 3), the manuscript states 'In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.' These are fundamentally incompatible test formats. The open-ended format allows for correct, misinformation-consistent, 'other,' and no-answer responses, while a two-alternative forced-choice format constrains responses to exactly two options. This contradiction makes it impossible to evaluate the scoring system, the dependent variables, or the appropriateness of the planned analyses.
issues.quote: The test will contain 20 open-ended questions, eight of which will cover all the critical details included in the movie... Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers (consistent with the movie), (2) answers consistent with the misinformation, (3) other answers... In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.

issues.description: The authors place all three interventions (Extended warning, Education about memory, Demonstration and motivation) AFTER the collaborative recall (misinformation phase) according to the procedure diagram and description in Section 2.5. However, in the Introduction (end of Section 1.1.4), the authors explicitly state: 'we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase (that is, before exposing participants to misinformation).' This is a direct contradiction about the temporal placement of the key experimental manipulation, which fundamentally affects the theoretical rationale and expected mechanisms of action.
issues.quote: What is important, we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase (that is, before exposing participants to misinformation)... After the discussion, there will be another filler task... After that, the third phase will take place: it will consist in the procedures to reduce vulnerability to misinformation

issues.subcategory: Lack of counterbalancing of discussed items
issues.description: The manuscript states that 'each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase.' This means that discussed vs. non-discussed items are not counterbalanced across pairs. Any differences between discussed and non-discussed items could be due to inherent differences in item difficulty, memorability, or salience rather than the effect of discussion/misinformation. This is a serious confound for the primary within-subjects comparison. The authors earlier state that 'discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced' in the Design section, which directly contradicts the Procedure section.
issues.quote: In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase. For example, all pairs will talk about Eric's cap color and his company logo.

issues.description: Section 2.3 (Design) states 'discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced,' but Section 2.5 (Procedure) states 'each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase.' These statements are mutually exclusive. If all pairs discuss the same four items, there is no counterbalancing of which items are discussed vs. non-discussed.
issues.quote: discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced... In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase.

issues.description: The control group listens to a podcast about 'soft skills related to social attitudes,' while the experimental groups receive interventions of varying content and format (podcasts, DRM task with feedback). The control podcast content could itself influence memory conformity (e.g., by priming social compliance or cooperation), and the different formats across conditions (passive listening vs. active DRM task) introduce confounds. A proper control should match the experimental conditions in format, duration, and cognitive engagement without containing the theoretically active ingredients.
issues.quote: In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes.

issues.subcategory: Unequal format and duration across conditions
issues.description: The Extended Warning and Education about memory conditions involve ~7-minute podcasts, while the Demonstration and motivation condition involves a DRM procedure (word lists, recall, feedback) PLUS a motivational podcast. The time, cognitive engagement, and format differ substantially across conditions, making it impossible to attribute differences to the theoretically active ingredients rather than to these procedural differences.
issues.quote: The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast... The training will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast... a substantially shortened and simplified procedure based on the DRM paradigm will be used... Afterwards, the participants will be motivated to resist illegitimate influences.

issues.description: The authors report a joint Hedges' g of 1.13 and convert this to Cohen's f of 'about 0.57.' For a within-subjects design, the conversion from g to f depends on the correlation between measures. Using the standard formula f = g/2 would give f = 0.565, which is close. However, for repeated-measures ANOVA, the relationship between d (or g) and f is f = d / (2 * sqrt(1)), which only holds under specific assumptions. More importantly, the correlation of 0.07 between discussed and non-discussed items is extremely low and unusual, which dramatically affects the power calculation. With r = 0.07, the effective sample size for detecting within-subjects effects is barely improved over a between-subjects design, yet the authors claim N = 18 is sufficient for 90% power. This warrants more careful verification.
issues.quote: the joint effect size, which was 1.13. This amounts to a Cohen f of about 0.57. The joint correlation of results in the discussed and non-discussed items in both studies available was 0.07. Under such conditions, the sample size required for 90% power was 18.

issues.subcategory: Heterogeneous effect sizes used without caution
issues.description: The two effect sizes used to estimate the memory conformity effect differ enormously: g = 1.92 (Ito et al., 2019) and g = 0.38 (Kękuś et al., 2020). The authors acknowledge this and use random effects, arriving at g = 1.13. However, with only two studies and such extreme heterogeneity (a 5-fold difference), the random-effects estimate is highly uncertain and the confidence interval would be extremely wide. Basing power analysis on this point estimate is unreliable. The authors should have acknowledged this uncertainty and perhaps powered for the smaller effect size to be conservative.
issues.quote: The existing results as regards effect sizes are Hedges' g = 1.92, N = 55 (Ito et al., 2019) and Hedges' g = 0.38, N = 74 (Kękuś et al., 2020). Given the rather large difference in effect sizes between both studies, random effects were assumed while calculating the joint effect size, which was 1.13.

issues.description: Participants are tested in pairs who watch the movie together and discuss details together. Members of a pair share the same collaborative recall experience, the same discussion dynamics, and potentially influence each other's subsequent test performance. The planned ANOVA treats individual participants as independent observations, but pair members are not independent. This violates the independence assumption of ANOVA and could inflate Type I error rates. The pair should be the unit of analysis, or multilevel modeling should be used to account for the nesting of individuals within pairs.
issues.quote: Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups... the participants (always a pair of them) will watch the movie about Eric.

issues.description: The manuscript states that pairs will be randomly assigned to conditions but provides no details about the randomization procedure (e.g., block randomization, stratification, who generates the random sequence, whether it is concealed). For a registered report, these procedural details are essential.
issues.quote: Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups

issues.description: There is no mention of experimenter blinding. The experimenter administers different interventions to different groups and is therefore aware of condition assignment. This could introduce demand characteristics or differential experimenter behavior across conditions. Given that the DRM condition requires active experimenter involvement (reading word lists, providing feedback), this is particularly concerning.
issues.quote: the experimenter will give the following information to the participants: 'Thank you for completing this memory task. Please take a look at your sheets now.'

issues.description: The exclusion criteria are extremely vague: 'We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session.' There are no criteria for excluding participants who notice the MORI manipulation (seeing both versions), who fail to engage in discussion, who have vision problems with polarized glasses, who fail attention/manipulation checks, or who show awareness of the study's true purpose. Previous MORI studies (e.g., Garry et al., 2008) excluded participants who noticed the dual projection, which is critical for the validity of the paradigm.
issues.quote: We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session.

issues.description: There is no manipulation check to verify that participants in the experimental conditions actually attended to, understood, or were affected by the interventions. For example, there is no check that participants in the Education condition learned about memory sins, or that participants in the Extended Warning condition understood the warning. Without manipulation checks, null results would be uninterpretable.

issues.subcategory: DRM effectiveness not validated for this purpose
issues.description: The Demonstration and motivation condition assumes that the DRM procedure will successfully produce false memories in most participants, which is then used as a demonstration of memory fallibility. However, the authors use only four word lists (a 'substantially shortened and simplified' version), and the effectiveness of such a brief DRM procedure is not established. If many participants do not produce false memories, the demonstration fails, and the manipulation is compromised.
issues.quote: a substantially shortened and simplified procedure based on the DRM paradigm will be used... Four lists will be chosen which on the basis of our previous research with this procedure, produce the strongest effect.

issues.description: The analysis plan specifies four indices from the individual memory test (correct answers, misinformation-consistent answers, other answers, overall number of answers) plus accuracy on filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions, plus subjective certainty ratings. Running ANOVAs on all these DVs without specifying a primary outcome or correction for multiple comparisons introduces substantial analytic flexibility and inflates the family-wise error rate.
issues.quote: We will explore the individual memory test's scores for the critical details using analysis of variance (ANOVA), using all four indices: the number of correct answers, number of answers consistent with misinformation, other answers, and the overall number of answers. Moreover, we will observe the individual memory test's average accuracy on the filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions.

issues.description: The analysis plan states that 'follow-up comparisons between pairs of groups will be performed' if the main interaction is significant, but does not specify which comparisons, what correction for multiple comparisons will be used, or whether these are planned contrasts vs. post-hoc tests. For a registered report, these details must be pre-specified.
issues.quote: In the case of a significant main interaction, follow-up comparisons between pairs of groups will be performed.

issues.subcategory: Ruling out normative influence without evidence
issues.description: The authors claim that normative influence is 'completely ruled out' because the individual memory test does not involve direct interpersonal pressure. However, normative influence can persist beyond the immediate social interaction. Participants may internalize social norms during the discussion phase, and these internalized norms can affect subsequent individual responses even without the partner present. The claim that normative influence is completely eliminated is too strong.
issues.quote: we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study: participants work on their own and do not compare their answers with anybody, therefore there is no cost of disagreeing.

issues.description: The theoretical rationale based on the IMP (Blank, 1998) focuses on participants who are 'aware of discrepancies' between original information and misinformation. The IMP framework was developed for post-warning (after misinformation). The Introduction states the interventions will be placed before collaborative recall to 'inoculate' participants, but the Procedure places them after. The theoretical mechanisms described (abandoning consistency assumption, detecting discrepancies) are post-misinformation mechanisms. If interventions are truly placed before misinformation, different mechanisms would be operative (e.g., enhanced encoding, increased vigilance during discussion), which are not theorized.
issues.quote: we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase... the participants who are aware of the discrepancy between both the original information and the misinformation obtained from the partner

issues.subcategory: Missing details on collaborative recall scoring
issues.description: The analysis plan describes how misinformation is classified during collaborative recall but does not specify how disagreements between partners during discussion will be handled analytically. The procedure notes 'If the participants are unable to reach an agreement, both responses will be documented,' but the analysis plan does not address how these cases will be treated—will they be counted as misinformation exposure or not?
issues.quote: If the participants are unable to reach an agreement, both responses will be documented.

issues.description: The sample is restricted to 16-35 year olds recruited via media and internet advertisements. This convenience sample may not generalize to actual eyewitnesses, who span all ages and demographics. The age restriction is justified only in terms of avoiding age-discrepant pairs, not in terms of the target population for eyewitness testimony. The authors do not acknowledge these limitations.
issues.quote: The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old; they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet.

issues.subcategory: Extended warning reveals deception before memory test
issues.description: The Extended Warning condition includes 'enlightenment regarding the purpose of the deception,' informing participants that their partner saw a different movie version. This fundamentally changes the task demands for this group compared to others—they now know the source of discrepancies. This is not merely a 'warning' but a complete revelation of the experimental manipulation, which could produce demand characteristics (participants trying to prove they weren't fooled) rather than genuine memory improvement. This confound is not addressed.
issues.quote: a clear warning that the partner might have been wrong during the collaborative recall... an enlightenment regarding the purpose of the deception.

issues.subcategory: No alpha level or directionality specified
issues.description: The analysis plan does not specify the significance level (alpha) to be used, despite mentioning 'directional significance tests.' For a registered report, the alpha level and whether one-tailed or two-tailed tests will be used must be pre-specified and justified.
issues.quote: Comparisons among all groups and directional significance tests are assumed.

issues.description: The theoretical framework heavily relies on the distinction between participants who are 'aware of discrepancies' between original information and misinformation versus those who are not. The authors predict that their methods will be effective primarily for aware participants. However, there is no measure of discrepancy awareness included in the procedure. Without this measure, the key theoretical prediction cannot be tested.
issues.quote: our methods are expected to be effective in terms of informational influence... we expect that effectiveness of our methods will be higher among people aware of discrepancies between the original information and misinformation than among those unaware of such discrepancies.

issues.description: The manuscript mentions several exploratory analyses (relationship between hypothesis awareness and performance, DRM results as predictor of MORI results) but does not clearly delineate confirmatory from exploratory analyses. For a registered report, this distinction is critical to prevent HARKing.
issues.quote: Their responses will be recorded for exploratory analysis of any relationship between hypothesis awareness and performance... the results on the DRM procedure will be used as a possible predictor of the results on the MORI technique.

issues.description: The analysis plan describes ANOVA but does not mention reporting effect sizes (e.g., partial eta-squared, Cohen's d) or confidence intervals for the results. Modern reporting standards require these.

issues.subcategory: Small number of critical items per condition
issues.description: There are only 8 critical details total, with 4 discussed and 4 non-discussed. This means each cell of the within-subjects factor has only 4 items, which severely limits reliability of the dependent measure and statistical power at the item level. Individual differences in item difficulty could have outsized effects.
issues.quote: the recording will be identical for each person in each pair, except for eight critical details... four of which refer to critical details

issues.subcategory: No plan for handling missing data or attrition
issues.description: The manuscript provides no plan for handling missing data, participant dropout, or cases where participants fail to complete all phases. There is no intention-to-treat analysis plan, no discussion of how partial data will be handled, and no anticipated attrition rate.

issues.subcategory: Podcast and intervention materials not provided
issues.description: The exact content of the podcasts (Extended Warning, Education about memory, control condition) and the DRM word lists are not provided or appended. For a registered report, the exact materials should be available for review to assess whether they operationalize the intended constructs and to enable replication.
issues.quote: The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast... The training will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast...

issues.subcategory: Control condition content may not be inert
issues.description: A podcast about 'soft skills related to social attitudes' could prime participants to be more socially compliant or agreeable, potentially increasing memory conformity in the control group. This would artificially inflate the apparent effectiveness of the experimental interventions. An inert control (e.g., nature documentary, unrelated factual content) would be more appropriate.
issues.quote: In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes.

issues.description: The authors acknowledge overlap between interventions ('teaching about memory is present in a way in both Education about memory and Demonstration and motivation') but dismiss this concern. Without factorial designs or component analyses, it is impossible to determine which elements of each intervention are responsible for any observed effects. The three interventions are not orthogonal, making comparative conclusions about mechanisms unwarranted.
issues.quote: we are aware of some overlap between the three interventions, for instance, teaching about memory is included is present in a way in both Education about memory and Demonstration and motivation. Empirical results may help to determine to what extent the overlap is substantial

issues.subcategory: MORI technique visual quality concerns not addressed
issues.description: The MORI technique is known to produce degraded image quality, particularly for one of the two versions (the one projected through the horizontal polarizer typically appears dimmer). This asymmetry can affect encoding quality differently for the two members of each pair. The manuscript does not discuss this known limitation or how it will be controlled (e.g., counterbalancing which version is shown through which polarizer).
issues.quote: The movie will be projected with two LED projectors placed such that the two images overlap on the screen. Polarizing filters will be placed in front of the lens of each projector: one will be oriented vertically and the other horizontally.

issues.subcategory: No specification of how subjective certainty data will be analyzed
issues.description: Participants rate subjective certainty (0-100%) for each answer, but the analysis plan never mentions how these data will be analyzed. Will certainty be a dependent variable? Will confidence-accuracy calibration be examined? This appears to be collected but not incorporated into the analysis plan.
issues.quote: for each question, the participants will be asked to rate the subjective certainty of each answer on a scale from 0% (complete uncertainty, guessing) to 100% (absolute certainty)

issues.subcategory: No check for MORI technique effectiveness
issues.description: There is no procedure to verify that participants did not detect the dual projection (i.e., that they believed they watched the same movie as their partner). While participants are asked about the study's purpose at the end, this is described as exploratory. A specific manipulation check for the MORI technique is standard in this literature and should be a formal exclusion criterion.
issues.quote: the subjects will be requested to say what they think the real purpose of the study was. Their responses will be recorded for exploratory analysis
